headline: Small caps' worst week in two years as Jio IPO closes at a record 22 times

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Saturday, the twenty-fourth of October, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most this morning. First, a bruising week on Dalal Street. The Nifty fell for a fourth straight session on Friday and closed below its two-hundred-week moving average, while mid-cap and small-cap stocks had their worst week in nearly two years. Around 25 lakh crore rupees of market value was wiped out in five days.

Second, the Jio Platforms IPO closed with a record book. It was subscribed a little over 22 times, and it is now India's largest public offer ever.

Third, oil. Brent crude is above 114 dollars a barrel, and that one number is weighing on the rupee, on bond yields and on every oil-sensitive stock. Let's get into it.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Friday was the fourth losing day in a row. The Nifty ended at about 22,600, down a little over half a percent, and the Sensex closed at 73,124. That was after a recovery from the day's lows, when the Sensex had fallen more than 1,300 points from its high.

The real damage was in the broader market. The small-cap index sank 2.6 percent on the day and the mid-cap index lost nearly 2.5 percent. Over the week, Business Standard says mid-caps fell 5.6 percent and small-caps 7.3 percent.

Realty and metals took the biggest beating. The Nifty Metal index has lost about 6 percent in four sessions. Capital goods fell nearly 4 percent, and Swiggy crashed after its results. IT was the one corner that held steady, close to flat. Oil-sensitive names such as BPCL, HPCL, IndiGo and the tyre makers fell up to 4 percent as crude climbed.

On flows, foreign institutional investors were net buyers of about 888 crore rupees on Friday, and domestic institutional investors bought about 3,459 crore rupees. This year so far, foreign investors have sold around 4.5 lakh crore rupees of Indian shares, while domestic institutions have bought more than 6.9 lakh crore rupees.

The fear gauge, India VIX, jumped about 6 percent to around 17. Now the levels. Moneycontrol's technical view says the Nifty could slip towards the 22,350 to 22,400 zone, and then 22,180, this month's low, in the coming monthly expiry week. Bank Nifty support is seen at 53,700. JM Financial says holding 22,000 could set up a rebound, but a break below it risks a fall towards 20,500.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
The Jio Platforms offer closed on Friday subscribed 22.19 times. Qualified institutional buyers bid for about 70.6 times their quota, and retail investors for about 2.7 times. Mint puts total bids at about 4.72 lakh crore rupees, and Moneycontrol says it is the first IPO anywhere to draw more than one crore applications. At about 30,200 crore rupees, it overtakes Hyundai Motor India as the country's biggest issue.

Friday also brought two very different debuts. Defence electronics maker Tonbo Imaging closed 62 percent above its issue price, while Zetwerk slid more than 20 percent.

One date for your calendar. EAAA India Alternatives opens its 1,200 crore rupee IPO on Monday, the twenty-sixth, at a price band of 1,585 to 1,665 rupees a share. It has raised 360 crore rupees from anchor investors.

In deals, UBS has taken a 4.8 percent stake in wealth manager 360 ONE WAM by converting warrants. And Welspun Corp won a 5,500 crore rupee gas pipeline order in the United States, taking its order book to a record 5.25 billion dollars.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
A busy Friday for results. Let's start with IT. Infosys grew its profit 6 percent to 7,823 crore rupees, on revenue of 49,244 crore rupees. Large deal wins were strong at 5.2 billion dollars. But it trimmed its full-year revenue growth guidance to 1 to 2 percent in constant currency, from 1.5 to 3 percent, and its American shares fell around 6 percent. Chief financial officer Jayesh Sanghrajka warned that pricing pressure will continue into the second half, as clients demand more productivity from AI. Infosys declared an interim dividend of 26 rupees a share.

Now to lenders. IndusInd Bank swung to a standalone profit of 1,176 crore rupees, from a loss of 445 crore a year ago, with gross bad loans down to 2.73 percent. Shriram Finance grew profit 59 percent to 3,677 crore rupees. And SBI Cards profit jumped 75 percent to 778 crore, as bad loan costs fell.

In metals, JSW Steel's profit jumped 225 percent to 5,279 crore rupees on record sales, though the stock fell about 3 percent. Jindal Steel's profit rose 21 percent to 771 crore, on record revenue of 19,448 crore rupees.

In energy, Adani Power's profit more than doubled to 6,919 crore rupees. BPCL's profit fell 21 percent to 4,863 crore, even as revenue rose 29 percent. The standalone refiners shone. Chennai Petroleum roughly tripled its profit to around 2,250 crore rupees, and MRPL's nearly tripled to 1,881 crore.

Tata Motors' commercial vehicle business posted a standalone profit of 2,138 crore rupees, with revenue up 42 percent. And Dr Reddy's profit fell 36 percent to 913 crore, on weakness in North America.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
The economy itself is holding up. The HSBC flash composite purchasing managers' index rose to 56.7 in October, a four-month high, led by services. Export orders grew at their fastest pace in six months, though hiring stalled. Business confidence rebounded too, with NCAER's index rising to 107.8 from 99.8.

But the strain from oil is showing. India's crude import bill jumped 46 percent to 90.6 billion dollars in April to September. Forex reserves fell about 5 billion dollars to 721 billion dollars in the week to the sixteenth of October, and Business Standard says they are down 65 billion dollars in six weeks. The rupee ended at 94.94 to the dollar, down 12 paise. Government bond yields have now risen for ten straight weeks, the worst losing streak in 30 years.

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said inflation is staying high while growth slows, and the RBI bulletin flagged inflation risks from the West Asia conflict and El Nino. At the same time, SBI Research says the RBI's 2.5 lakh crore rupee liquidity injection sends mixed signals while it is tightening policy. The governor also repeated that upper-layer non-bank lenders must list, which keeps the spotlight on Tata Sons.

On the brighter side, net foreign direct investment rose to 13.8 billion dollars in April to August, from 9.6 billion a year ago. And disinvestment secretary Arunish Chawla said the government will keep cutting its stake in public sector banks towards 75 percent.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Oil is the story globally too. Brent is above 114 dollars a barrel. Mohammed Imran of Mirae Asset Sharekhan links the latest jump to a deadly drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field. He notes crude is up about 85 percent this year, and says Brent may hit 120 dollars.

Higher oil and rising US bond yields have hit precious metals. Mint reports silver is down about 56,000 rupees a kilo from its August peak, and gold is down around 23,000 rupees per ten grams.

On energy diplomacy, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called India a refining superpower, as Washington looks to Indian refineries to process Venezuelan crude. Refiners, though, tell Business Standard that American barrels stay costly because of record freight rates. Next week brings the US Federal Reserve's rate decision, and the US midterm elections follow on the third of November.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
First, an investor warning. The market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has ordered Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy and its founder to refund about 546 crore rupees, plus about 68 crore rupees of interest. The money was collected for unregistered investment advice and stock recommendations, given through paid courses and WhatsApp groups. The regulator also levied penalties of 11.5 crore rupees and barred them from the market for two years.

On tax, the new Form 141 under the Income-tax Act of 2025 replaces four TDS forms. From this tax year, it covers TDS on property purchases, rent, payments to contractors and professionals, and transfers of virtual digital assets.

If a UPI payment fails but the money leaves your account, RBI rules require the bank to refund it within a set time, and to pay 100 rupees a day as compensation for any delay.

For Yes Bank's AT1 bondholders, the Supreme Court has overturned the 2020 write-off, but Mint reports the bank is unlikely to pay this year's coupons and may seek a review. And with Dhanteras near, remember that a BIS hallmark certifies the purity of the gold, not the diamonds or stones set in it. Bank branches are closed today, the fourth Saturday.

That's the brief. Markets are shut for the weekend, so here is what to watch next week. Jio share allotment on Monday and its listing on Wednesday. The EAAA India Alternatives IPO opening on Monday. The monthly derivatives expiry, with the Nifty sitting near key support levels. And above all, crude oil and the US Federal Reserve. Have a restful weekend, and I'll be back with you tomorrow.
